links.outcome: Head-to-head LVO detection performance of two commercial AI tools versus neuroradiologist consensus
links.effect: AUROC 0.93 for both tools (p = 0.64); at matched 83% sensitivity, JLK LVO specificity 0.96 vs RAPID CTA 0.89.
links.quote: Both tools demonstrated high and comparable overall performance (AUROC 0.93 for both, p = 0.64).

links.outcome: Local retrospective validation of AI LVO detection against expert reference standard
links.effect: In 176 consecutive local patients, both tools achieved AUROC 0.93 against neuroradiologist consensus; misclassification causes reviewed.
links.quote: The performance of RAPID CTA and JLK LVO was compared against expert neuroradiologist consensus using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).

unlisted_practices: Review of false-positive and false-negative cases to identify common pitfalls (high-grade stenosis mimics, collateral flow masking distal occlusions)

screen.reason: Retrospective comparative evaluation and failure analysis of two commercial AI tools for detecting large vessel occlusions on CTA, without testing a deployment safeguard or organizational practice.
